# StableToolBench
**Type:** Measurement  
**Referenced in:** 6 papers  

## State of the Field

**What it is.** Across the papers, StableToolBench is most commonly described as a benchmark for evaluating tool invocation or the accuracy of function calls generated by models. Some descriptions stay at that level, while others characterize it more specifically as a stable version of the Rapid-API access system derived from ToolBench, using an API caching mechanism; those papers also describe it as containing 765 solvable tasks or questions across six subsets or subtasks, varying in tool category and instruction complexity from single-tool to multi-tool instructions, and featuring a virtual API server and stable evaluation system.

**What it is claimed to measure.** Papers link the benchmark to a narrow set of targets rather than many distinct outcomes: it is linked to one behavioral indicator, Tool use, and one construct, Generalization. One paper uses it to measure Tool use, operationalized through the "accuracy of function calls" on StableToolBench, and another reports using real-world tool benchmarks including this one to evaluate generalization ability.

**Space of uses.** In use, papers position StableToolBench as an evaluation benchmark within broader benchmark suites and direct model comparisons. One study compares function-call accuracy for ToolLlama and two one-shot baselines on it, while others report experiments on StableToolBench together with RestBench-TMDB, or evaluate it alongside BFCL, GSM8K, and MATH; no measurement instrument is linked to it.
